The guard that guarded nothing

PR playground for #4025. Two tests dirtied the tree. Then my guard against them turned out to be vacuous.

The dangerous one

On any machine without NPM_TOKEN, test-mdx-compile.sh hits a 401 and swaps the real manifest:

-  "@yonatan-hq/analytics": "^1.2.0",
+  "@yonatan-hq/analytics": "file:../stubs/analytics-stub"

Then npm rewrites the real lockfile beside it. The test passes, says nothing about the tree, and a developer who ran the suite before committing stages a no-op analytics for a live site without noticing. git status is the only witness, and this is the defect that makes git status untrustworthy.

The pointless one

test-skill-tokens.sh rewrote a tracked baseline on every run, stamping a fresh generated_at each time. Nothing anywhere reads that file. It is written by that script and read by nobody, so the churn bought exactly zero. Now opt-in via SKILL_TOKENS_WRITE_BASELINE=1.

And then my own guard failed the same way

The first draft compared whole-tree git status before and after, and skipped when the tree was already dirty. Which is exactly the situation it exists for.

ARM 1: revert the skill-tokens gate   FAIL: stayed green
       (the revert dirtied the tree, the guard skipped, asserted nothing)

A guard that only works on a perfectly clean tree is a guard that rarely works. It now hashes the three at-risk files by name, which works mid-change, needs no skip path, and cannot fail open. Unrelated edits are invisible to it by construction.

Both arms, after the fix

ARM 1: revert the skill-tokens gate   went red  (on a DIRTY tree, deliberately)
ARM 2: remove the mdx EXIT trap       went red
restored                              green, 4/4
bash tests/unit/test-suite-leaves-tree-clean.sh

Two assertions on the mdx side, not one

A restore that exists but is never trapped runs on the happy path and nowhere else, which leaves the swap behind on precisely the failure paths that matter. So the guard checks that a restore is defined and that it is wired to EXIT.

The mdx assertion is structural, and labelled as such rather than dressed up: that test runs npm ci against docs/site and takes minutes, so running it inside a fast unit guard would get the guard deleted. It catches the regression that matters, someone removing the restore, without the cost.
